title: What's a Sandal Doing Up a Tree?

collection.credit: NEW EVENTS — WHAT'S THAT DOING HERE? (WD-01 to WD-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)

ledger.why: the casting line (the roles carry it)
the owner's naming rule (2026-11-15): a person the draft names by role is a cast villager, named at the first mention

collection.description: A single sandal hangs in the tree outside a villager's hut, and nobody is missing one: get it down, or leave it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: There's a sandal in the tree outside (subject)'s hut. Just one. It's caught on a branch, well above head height, swinging gently in the breeze. (subject) checks (subject.his/her) own feet. Both sandals. (subject.He/She) checks with (friend). Both sandals. Nobody in the village seems to be missing a sandal. It just hangs there.

a.name: Answer A
a.text: (subject) climbs the tree and fetches it down. It's a perfectly good sandal. It doesn't fit anybody. (subject.He/She) puts it by the path in case its owner comes looking. Nobody ever does. After a week, (child), a child, starts using it as a boat for a crab. That, everyone agrees, is a good use for a sandal with no story.

b.name: Answer B
b.text: (subject) decides the sandal has chosen its spot. Soon the whole village knows it as "the sandal tree," and gives directions by it: "past the sandal tree, then left." When a storm finally knocks the sandal down months later, people keep calling it the sandal tree anyway.
